result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.cmty_fluid()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Find k communities with the asynchronous fluid communities algorithm. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.cmty_fluid()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Find k communities with the asynchronous fluid communities algorithm. title: >- [Graph.cmty_fluid()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Find k communities with the asynchronous fluid communities algorithm. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find `k` communities with the asynchronous fluid communities algorithm. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L36136-L36217){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.cmty_fluid( k, max_iter=100, seed=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Fluid communities](../assets/graphs/cmty-fluid.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense four-node groups, A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, joined by the single edge D to E. Asked for k = 2 communities with seed 3, two fluids start at random nodes and spread until each fills one group, drawn as tinted regions in the accent color and teal. The card lists community 0 as A, B, C, D and community 1 as E, F, G, H." width="100%"} Fluid communities (Parés et al., 2017) treat each community as a fluid that starts at a random node with total density 1 and spreads over the graph: nodes repeatedly join the community with the largest total density among themselves and their neighbors, while each community's density is spread thinner as it grows. Communities expand and compete until nothing changes. It is one of the few fast methods that lets you choose the number of communities directly, useful when the number of groups is known in advance (teams, districts, servers to balance across). The graph must be undirected and connected. Results depend on the random start; use `seed=` for reproducibility. Edge weights are not used. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The number of communities (between 1 and the number of nodes). [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of passes over the nodes (default 100). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute to store the communities in (default `"cmty_fluid"`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the node-to-community dictionary instead of storing it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : With `return_dict=True`, a dictionary mapping node IDs to community labels `0` to `k - 1` (numbered in order of the lowest node ID in each); otherwise `self`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected, or `k` is out of range. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Each pass visits the nodes in random order; a node's score for community `c` is the sum of `c`'s density $1 / |c|$ over the node and its neighbors in `c`, and the node switches only if its current community is not among the (near-)best. Each pass costs $O(E)$. Follows NetworkX's `asyn_fluidc`; with a different random generator, the communities found for a given seed differ from NetworkX's. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two dense groups joined by a single edge split cleanly into two fluids: ::: {#47c1222f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEFGH")) g.add_edges( [("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("E", "F"), ("E", "G"), ("E", "H"), ("F", "G"), ("F", "H"), ("G", "H"), ("D", "E")] ) groups = g.cmty_fluid(2, seed=3, return_dict=True) {g.get_label_from_id(n): c for n, c in sorted(groups.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0, 'B': 0, 'C': 0, 'D': 0, 'E': 1, 'F': 1, 'G': 1, 'H': 1} ``` ::: :::
